official.application_cycle: 2027 delivery - Cohort 1: 25 January - 5 March 2027; Cohort 2: 15 March - 23 April 2027
official.status_note: The official programme page states 'Applications are open' and 'Open for applications until 12 October 2026, at 11:00 (UTC)'.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The programme page states each fellowship includes 'Full programme fees'.
benefits: Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship, including pre-arranged accommodation close to Oxford
Arrival allowance loaded onto the cash card (per the official Fellows' FAQ on funding and money)
Contribution towards the cost of a TB test where one is required for the UK visa application
eligibility: Be a citizen of and resident in one of the following countries at the point of application: Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Holy See, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, or Switzerland.
Hold a postgraduate qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field).
Have at least five years' relevant professional experience.

Be a mid-career professional with responsibilities for national or international security, employed within government, public or private sector, academia, defence, security, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, or an international organisation.
Be working in a role with the potential to influence organisational capability, policy, strategy, or operational effectiveness within their organisation and/or country.

Be able to demonstrate leadership potential and a commitment to applying the knowledge and networks gained through the fellowship within their organisation and/or country on completion of the programme.
requirements: Meet the general Chevening Fellowship eligibility criteria and all programme-specific requirements.
Apply through the Chevening online application system reached from the 'APPLY TODAY' link on the programme page.
Return to your country of citizenship (country of award) for at least one year after your fellowship ends.
Not hold British or dual British citizenship (unless you are a citizen of a British Overseas Territory).
Not have received UK Government scholarship funding (including Chevening) within the last five years.
selection_criteria: Demonstrate the potential to rise to a position of leadership and influence.
Demonstrate the personal, intellectual, and interpersonal attributes reflecting this potential.
Meet all programme-specific fellowship eligibility requirements for the Europe Defence and Security Fellowship.
Assessed as a mid-career professional whose role can influence organisational capability, policy, strategy, or operational effectiveness.
coverage: Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship, including pre-arranged accommodation close to Oxford
application_method: Confirm citizenship of and residence in one of the 35 listed European countries at the point of application.
Apply through the Chevening online application system via the 'APPLY TODAY' link on the programme page (asams.chevening.org/apply).
official.application_route: Apply online through the Chevening application system (asams.chevening.org/apply) via the APPLY TODAY link on the official programme page, before 11:00 (UTC) on 12 October 2026.
official.citizenship_residency: Be a citizen of and resident in one of 35 listed European countries at the point of application; applicants living in a European overseas territory apply through the relevant Chevening award scheme for the European country of which they are a citizen.
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants who are citizens of and resident in the 35 listed European countries; the programme page states it is open to all non-ODA eligible European countries.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Mid-career professionals with responsibilities for national or international security, employed within government, public or private sector, academia, defence, security, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, or an international organisation; the page lists relevant sectors including military and civilian defence staff, government officials and diplomats, cybersecurity/technology specialists, energy and infrastructure professionals, and journalists, researchers and academics working on relevant issues.
official.research_requirement: Throughout the programme fellows work on a research project addressing a relevant policy, leadership, organisational, or security challenge, and present their findings to the FCDO in London at the end of the fellowship.
official.duration: Six weeks, in two cohorts: Cohort 1: 25 January - 5 March 2027; Cohort 2: 15 March - 23 April 2027
official.description: Funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and delivered by Cranfield University at the Defence Academy of the United Kingdom, Shrivenham, the Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship is designed for mid-career professionals from across Europe who have demonstrated leadership potential in security and defence. Through six weeks of teaching, discussion, practical exercises, site visits, individual research and collaborative learning, fellows develop practical insight into leadership, organisational resilience, governance, strategic decision-making, cyber resilience, artificial intelligence and international collaboration.

verification.notes: Programme, eligibility and FAQ pages on chevening.org were read directly on 2026-10-10; the stipend value is not published and is confirmed in the Final Award Letter after selection, so amount fields are null.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a six-week, fully covered FCDO fellowship for mid-career European defence and security professionals, hosted by Cranfield University at Shrivenham, with fees, accommodation close to Oxford, living expenses and return airfare all paid. No monetary value is published - the stipend is only spelled out in the Final Award Letter after you are selected, so budget blind. Applications close at 11:00 UTC on 12 October 2026 through the Chevening online system, so the window is essentially shut by the time most applicants read this. If you are a citizen and resident of one of the 35 listed European countries with five years' security-relevant experience and employer backing, this is one of the few UK-funded routes that covers the full cost of a short leadership programme.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career defence, security, intelligence, policing or civil-protection professionals based in one of the 35 listed European countries who hold a postgraduate qualification and can be released by their employer for six weeks.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your citizenship and current residence against the 35-country list - residency at the point of application, not just nationality, is checked.
Confirm your employer will release you for six weeks (either the January-March or March-April 2027 cohort) before you apply.
Check you hold no British or dual British citizenship and have taken no UK Government scholarship funding in the past five years.
Have your employment history ready to demonstrate five years of relevant professional experience across up to fifteen employment periods.
Prepare to present the research project you would develop during the fellowship, since findings are presented to the FCDO in London at the end of the programme.
common_rejection_risks: Residency mismatch: being a citizen of a listed country but resident elsewhere at the point of application disqualifies you.
Falling short of the five-year relevant professional experience threshold stated on the programme page.
Holding British or dual British citizenship, or having had UK Government scholarship funding within the last five years.
Being an employee or relative of an employee of HMG, the British Council or a sponsoring UK university, which voids eligibility.
Employer refusal to release you for the six-week programme once selected.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Dependant costs are not funded by Chevening; the programme page and FAQ do not publish the stipend value, so personal spending beyond the living allowance, any pre-arrival expenses before the arrival allowance starts, and personal travel arranged outside the official provider are borne by the fellow.
document_audit: The official pages publish no document checklist for this programme, so do not assume a reference or CV upload will be accepted late - complete every section of the online form in one sitting before the deadline.

A TB test contribution applies only where a TB test is required for your UK visa application; check your country's requirement early because visa processing time sits between selection and the January/March cohort start.
Some fellowships include international or domestic travel during the programme, but only the course outline from the host university confirms this for your cohort - do not budget on assumptions.
alerts: The deadline of 11:00 (UTC) on 12 October 2026 is only days after the verification date of this record - treat the window as effectively closed for this cycle and watch the find-a-programme page for the next round.
There are two cohorts (25 January - 5 March and 15 March - 23 April 2027); taking the later cohort shortens the gap between an October decision and departure but leaves less visa preparation time.
You must return to your country of citizenship for at least one year after the fellowship ends - this rules out any plan to stay in the UK afterwards.
Extensions are granted only in exceptional circumstances and are subject to funding; Chevening states they are not automatic.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete and submit the Chevening online fellowship application at asams.chevening.org/apply via the APPLY TODAY link before 11:00 (UTC) on 12 October 2026; selection then proceeds through Chevening's fellowship assessment before offers and acceptance.
